numerical_failure.observed_behavior: With check_dtype=False and check_exact=False, comparing an int64 Series containing 2**60 + 1 against a float64 Series containing 2.0**60 raises no AssertionError, because array_equivalent() casts the large integer to float64 and returns early, so atol and rtol are never applied; the values are 1 apart with atol=0.5.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: pd.testing.assert_series_equal should raise AssertionError, since the integer values differ by 1 which exceeds atol=0.5 with rtol=0; the tolerance should be applied to the exact integer values rather than to values cast to float64.
trigger_conditions: comparing an integer dtype operand against a float dtype operand
large integer values beyond float64 exact precision (e.g. 2**60 + 1)
non-zero atol or rtol supplied (rtol=0, atol=0.5 in reproducer)
rtol >= 0 and atol >= 0 for the new local path

input_output_examples.input: left = pd.Series([2**60 + 1], dtype="int64"); right = pd.Series([float(2**60)], dtype="float64"); pd.testing.assert_series_equal(left, right, check_dtype=False, check_exact=False, rtol=0, atol=0.5)

oracle_clues: expected message format from patch: f"expected {ib}.00000 but got {ia}.00000, with rtol={rtol}, atol={atol}"
issue reproducer comment: no AssertionError, even though the values are 1 apart and atol is 0.5
whatsnew entry: fixed bug in testing.assert_series_equal ignoring rtol and atol when comparing large integer and floating dtypes with check_dtype=False (GH#66699)

numerical_characteristics.dtype: int64 and float64 (mixed integer/float comparison; check_dtype=False); uint64 vs float64 also appears in tests
numerical_characteristics.precision: float64 cannot represent the one-integer difference at large magnitudes; integer precision is lost when a large integer is cast to float64
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: values near 2**53 and above, e.g. 2**60 + 1 vs float(2**60), 2**63 + 1 vs float(2**63), 2**53 + 1 vs float(2**53)
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: rtol=0, atol=0.5 (the difference of 1 must fail) and atol=1 (must pass); rtol and atol are applied to exact integer values
category_specific_evidence: Issue #66699: pd.Series([2**60 + 1], dtype='int64') vs pd.Series([float(2**60)], dtype='float64') with check_dtype=False, check_exact=False, rtol=0, atol=0.5 gives no AssertionError although values differ by 1.
array_equivalent() casts the integer and float operands to float64 and returns early before tolerance logic runs, losing integer precision.

PR #66722 handles the precision-sensitive case locally in pandas/_libs/testing.pyx without changing array_equivalent(), using int(a) and int(b) comparisons when the float operand is an integer value and rtol>=0, atol>=0.
Tests in test_assert_almost_equal.py parametrize large mixed int/float cases (2**60+1, 2**53+1, -(2**53)-1, uint64 2**63+1) asserting not-almost-equal at atol=0.5 and almost-equal at atol=1.
Discussion suggests the rtol>=0 and atol>=0 check should come first as the cheapest condition.
Same-dtype integer case is addressed separately by PR #66696 and not duplicated here.
reproduction_risks: Reproduction must use check_dtype=False and check_exact=False, otherwise the path differs.
Float64 casting of the integer happens in array_equivalent before tolerance logic; the bug only appears on the mixed int/float path.
Validation counts from the PR (300 passed, 2 xfailed; 8 passed with PR #66696) are version-specific and not reproduction targets.
